title: Single-entry global decode/encode cache in net/encoding.py
answers: Is there a per-message cache of decoded body?
body:
- Cache is module-global `_cache = CachedDecode(encoded, encoding, errors, decoded)` (namedtuple) in `mitmproxy/net/encoding.py`; process-wide, ONE entry.
- `decode()` hit: input is bytes and encoded/encoding/errors all equal cache → returns `_cache.decoded`. `encode()` checks the reverse (decoded equal → returns `_cache.encoded`), so an encode also primes a decode hit (round trip avoids recompression).
- Only updated for gzip, deflate, deflateraw, br, zstd; identity/text codecs never cached.
- `Message` (http.py) keeps no decoded copy; each `.content` access calls encoding.decode and relies on this cache. Keyed by full-body equality, so cost scales with body size; alternating between two bodies thrashes it.
